extraction.body: Bitcoin 's latest sell-off is reviving doubts that it can behave as the "digital gold" market hedge that crypto backers have long envisioned. Coming into 2026, experts said that showing bitcoin could serve as a market hedge rather than a risk-on asset that moves up and down with growth stocks was an important test for the cryptocurrency. Bitcoin was trading under $62,000 on Friday morning, down from an all-time high of more than $126,000 in early October last year. Its downward spiral in recent months and weeks has been precipitated by a confluence of factors. The heavy midterm elections losses for the Republicans, the Binance hack, and a world on edge about the security of all things technology — FAA ground stop, the outage of the National Security Agency's highly classified internal communications system, several online banking outages — have not helped the mood when it comes to putting trust in the digital world. But the market itself may be the biggest factor. Investors are currently in sell everything mode, including tech stocks and gold — the Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 tumbled into correction territory on Friday, according to CNBC data. Bitcoin's recent price action has also tracked the move in the biggest tech IPOs , SpaceX and Anthropic. Taken together, the cryptocurrency is failing the test again when it comes to showing its worth as a market hedge during times of investor anxiety. In the past month alone, bitcoin had dropped roughly $20,000, as of Friday morning, according to CNBC data. Investors and financial management firms aren't viewing it as safe an investment as in the past, said Ryan Kirkley, co-founder and chief executive of Global Settlement Network, a Miami-based fintech that provides infrastructure for currency settlement, including crypto. "There's a bit more caution than there was a year ago." What is behind bitcoin's fall, and what is in store for its future? Here is what experts say. There have been many theories about how bitcoin would react based on different market and economic conditions. But historically, bitcoin has done best in low-rate environments and when lending opportunities are plentiful, said Juan Xavier Sanchez, head of wealth strategy at Activest Wealth Management in Aventura, Florida. When rates are down and treasuries aren't paying good yields, people tend to be more risk-seeking for higher returns. "Bitcoin for many investors is in that bucket," Sanchez said. Experts have noted that gold, which is now down over 35% from its early 2026 peak, is less attractive when cash accounts are paying 5%. Investments like gold and bitcoin offer no yield. Bitcoin's rising correlation with the Nasdaq-100 since late September suggests the two are increasingly moving in tandem, according to data from Fairlead Strategies, a technical research firm. That's consistent with an environment of higher volatility in which correlations across risk assets tend to increase. However, the correlation remains below its early-2026 highs, the data show. Bitcoin has certain characteristics of digital gold, in that it has a limited supply, no single owner and no CEO or board that can decide to issue more, said Anthony Georgiades, founder and general partner at Innovating Capital in New York, which invests in early-stage crypto, blockchain, digital infrastructure and deep tech companies. But it's also been caught up in monetary policy since its inception. The last decade or so of monetary policy has been extremely rewarding to speculative risk-on assets, Georgiades said. However, in periods of volatility, those types of assets have experienced the most significant drawdowns and have been the most heavily punished, Georgiades said. That means that a shock on one side of the board that might be completely independent of bitcoin could trigger a large volatility event "given how intertwined digital assets have become in the overall financial system," he said. Notably, bitcoin hasn't acted much like digital gold in more recent years, said Abe Sheikh, chief investment officer of Cordoba Advisory Partners in New York. In fact, it has fallen substantially during periods when the stock market has been falling. For example, from October 6 through November 18, the S&P 500 fell about 6.3%, and bitcoin fell around 27%. From January 21, 2025 through April 8, 2025, the S&P dropped around 17.4%, while bitcoin slid 27.8%, he said. Democrats gaining control over both houses is viewed as a negative for crypto from a market perspective. The crypto industry spent more than $200 million to support crypto-friendly candidates, but its role had less of an impact on overall results than in the last election cycle. However, bitcoin's downward trend was already in the works, said Cyrus Amini, chief investment officer at Hyphen Wealth Management in Lafayette, California. In September, the Clarity Act failed in the U.S. Senate, and while its outlook is now dim , according to many political and market experts, some form of crypto legislation is still considered a priority for many Democrats and Republicans, while the Trump-appointed heads of the Commodity Future Trading Commission and Securities and Exchange Commission continue to favor crypto in rulemaking. This fall, investors also started to question the security of encryption technology, leading to more concerns over the security of their bitcoin holdings, said Kirkley of Global Settlement Network. The Binance hack in October muddied the waters further. And the recent stock market jitters and economic concerns piled on doubts, Kirkley said. The last few weeks have been especially rough with data security concerns from multiple fronts, he added. Wall Street's embrace of bitcoin has been a big positive for the cryptocurrency. Kirkley noted that 20% of bitcoin's market price is coming from institutional investors, and that's a conservative estimate. In addition, new research from digital assets company Galaxy shows that a record 40.5% of all 13F-reported spot bitcoin exchange-traded product holdings, and 11.2% of all the bitcoin in the funds, came from advisory and wealth planning firms, such as RIAs and brokerage platforms, as of the third quarter 13F filings with the SEC, which are required of firms with over $100 million in assets to report their holdings. Much of this investment is through bitcoin spot ETFs like the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) that track its price. These ETFs, first approved by the SEC in January 2024, were supposed to provide a reliable new source of institutional demand. But ETF ownership also makes bitcoin especially easy to sell. Outflows from several of these funds have been substantial in recent months. IBIT, the largest of its peers, had six-month net outflows of $1.65 billion through Nov. 18 and one-month outflows of $1.37 billion, according to ETF Database. The second biggest, Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund ( FBTC ) had one-month net outflows of $322.65 million and six-month net outflows of $771.86 million, according to ETF Database. Grayscale Bitcoin Mini Trust ETF ( BTC ) had one-month net outflows of $66.35 million, though it had inflows of $590.04 million over six months. As of September 2026, public companies collectively hold close to 1.29 million bitcoins, which is more than 6% of the 21 million coins in existence, according to bitcoin.com . Most public companies invest their corporate treasury portfolios in low-risk, highly liquid instruments such as money market funds, Treasury bonds and Treasury bills. That said, there are some well-known companies that have invested in bitcoin. SpaceX, for example, purchased 18,712 bitcoins for a total cost of $661 million, at an average price of $35,324 per coin. The company began accumulating bitcoin in early 2021 and held its position unchanged from mid-2024 until its IPO filing . Digital Asset Treasury companies, known as DATs or DATCOs, have also played a role in bitcoin's volatility . DATs are publicly listed firms whose primary business strategy involves holding significant quantities of digital assets, such as bitcoin or ethereum , on their corporate balance sheets to drive shareholder value. Companies in this space include Strategy , Strive, and Twenty One Capital. "DATs have exacerbated the problem," said Sheikh of Cordoba Advisory Partners. When bitcoin is rising, these companies borrow money in the debt market or raise capital to buy more bitcoin, which magnifies the upswings. They have also sold bitcoin to make their bond coupon payments. "It leads to enormous volatility on the upside and downside," Sheikh said. As of mid-November, Strategy, the largest corporate holder of bitcoin, holds 850,849 BTC, according to a regulatory filing . That represents roughly 4% of bitcoin's total supply. The company acquired these holdings at a total cost of approximately $64.2 billion, with an average purchase price of roughly $75,452 per coin, according to the filing. Bitcoin has been trending lower since the peak in October 2025. A trading range has taken hold and the bottom of the range is just below 60,000, said Katie Stockton, founder and managing partner of Fairlead Strategies. "It appears to be trying to find a footing," she said. Oversold conditions on the heels of recent lows in June and July, in addition to long-term momentum, suggest bitcoin can support an upturn, she said. But that depends on whether the crypto can hold at a current range around $60,000, she said. "At the end of the day, bitcoin is exceptionally volatile. It's still an area that people might go to sell when they think that risk is higher in other areas." By mid-morning Friday, the price of bitcoin had slipped below $60,000, its lowest mark since July. It was on pace for its seventh-straight weekly loss for the first time since May 2022, according to CNBC data.

The company began accumulating bitcoin in early 2021 and held its position unchanged from mid-2024 until its IPO filing .

Digital Asset Treasury companies, known as DATs or DATCOs, have also played a role in bitcoin's volatility . DATs are publicly listed firms whose primary business strategy involves holding significant quantities of digital assets, such as bitcoin or ethereum , on their corporate balance sheets to drive shareholder value. Companies in this space include Strategy , Strive, and Twenty One Capital.

"DATs have exacerbated the problem," said Sheikh of Cordoba Advisory Partners. When bitcoin is rising, these companies borrow money in the debt market or raise capital to buy more bitcoin, which magnifies the upswings. They have also sold bitcoin to make their bond coupon payments. "It leads to enormous volatility on the upside and downside," Sheikh said.

As of mid-November, Strategy, the largest corporate holder of bitcoin, holds 850,849 BTC, according to a regulatory filing . That represents roughly 4% of bitcoin's total supply. The company acquired these holdings at a total cost of approximately $64.2 billion, with an average purchase price of roughly $75,452 per coin, according to the filing.

Bitcoin has been trending lower since the peak in October 2025. A trading range has taken hold and the bottom of the range is just below 60,000, said Katie Stockton, founder and managing partner of Fairlead Strategies. "It appears to be trying to find a footing," she said.

Oversold conditions on the heels of recent lows in June and July, in addition to long-term momentum, suggest bitcoin can support an upturn, she said. But that depends on whether the crypto can hold at a current range around $60,000, she said. "At the end of the day, bitcoin is exceptionally volatile. It's still an area that people might go to sell when they think that risk is higher in other areas."

By mid-morning Friday, the price of bitcoin had slipped below $60,000, its lowest mark since July. It was on pace for its seventh-straight weekly loss for the first time since May 2022, according to CNBC data.

extraction.body: Bitcoin fell sharply on Thursday, dropping below $85,000 for the first time in nearly two months, as a broad pullback in risk assets swept through global markets and intensified pressure on cryptocurrencies. The world’s largest digital asset slid as much as 5.7% to $84,233, its lowest level since Dec. 1. The decline marked a significant breakdown after weeks of sideways trading and underscored the fragility of sentiment across the crypto market. Losses were even steeper among smaller tokens, with Ether, XRP, Dogecoin, Cardano and Solana all falling by 6% or more. The sharp move lower in prices triggered a wave of forced selling across crypto derivatives markets. Around $785 million worth of digital assets were liquidated over the past 24 hours, according to data compiled by Coinglass. More than half of those liquidations occurred in just the last four hours, reflecting the speed at which losses cascaded as key technical levels were breached. The latest drop extended a broader downturn that has persisted in crypto markets since early October. Bitcoin prices had largely stagnated in recent weeks, even as technology stocks and precious metals such as gold and silver rallied. That divergence broke down abruptly, however, as cryptocurrencies began to mirror a wider selloff in risk assets. Technology stocks led the decline, with Microsoft shares collapsing more than 11%, a move that would rank as their worst one-day fall since March 2020. The selloff followed the company’s report of slowing growth in its cloud business and dragged the Nasdaq Composite lower by roughly 1.5%, reinforcing a risk-off tone across markets. The pressure was not limited to equities. Precious metals, which had surged to record highs, also reversed violently. Gold, which had briefly climbed above $5,600 per ounce earlier in the session — having never traded above $5,000 before Sunday night — plunged nearly 10% within minutes during US morning trade, falling back below $5,200. Silver followed a similar trajectory, sliding from around $121 per ounce to $108. Bitcoin exchange-traded funds have also come under strain. So far this week, bitcoin ETFs have recorded $160.1 million in net outflows, according to data from SoSoValue, extending a pattern of capital leaving the products amid market turbulence. Julio Moreno, head of research at CryptoQuant, said the recent pullback represents the first meaningful stress test for bitcoin ETFs since their rapid growth last year. Moreno noted that cumulative ETF flows peaked at $72.6 billion on Oct. 10, 2025, and have since seen $6.1 billion in net outflows. That reduction has cut ETF holdings to about $66.5 billion, representing an 8.4% drawdown from the peak. “If price holds above ETF realized price, it gives this cohort a reason to stay invested. extraction.body: Bitcoin 's latest sell-off is reviving doubts that it can behave as the "digital gold" market hedge that crypto backers have long envisioned. Coming into 2026, experts said that showing bitcoin could serve as a market hedge rather than a risk-on asset that moves up and down with growth stocks was an important test for the cryptocurrency. Bitcoin was trading under $62,000 on Friday morning, down from an all-time high of more than $126,000 in early October last year. Its downward spiral in recent months and weeks has been precipitated by a confluence of factors. The heavy midterm elections losses for the Republicans, the Binance hack, and a world on edge about the security of all things technology — FAA ground stop, the outage of the National Security Agency's highly classified internal communications system, several online banking outages — have not helped the mood when it comes to putting trust in the digital world. But the market itself may be the biggest factor. Investors are currently in sell everything mode, including tech stocks and gold — the Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 tumbled into correction territory on Friday, according to CNBC data. Bitcoin's recent price action has also tracked the move in the biggest tech IPOs , SpaceX and Anthropic. Taken together, the cryptocurrency is failing the test again when it comes to showing its worth as a market hedge during times of investor anxiety. In the past month alone, bitcoin had dropped roughly $20,000, as of Friday morning, according to CNBC data. Investors and financial management firms aren't viewing it as safe an investment as in the past, said Ryan Kirkley, co-founder and chief executive of Global Settlement Network, a Miami-based fintech that provides infrastructure for currency settlement, including crypto. "There's a bit more caution than there was a year ago." What is behind bitcoin's fall, and what is in store for its future? Here is what experts say. There have been many theories about how bitcoin would react based on different market and economic conditions. But historically, bitcoin has done best in low-rate environments and when lending opportunities are plentiful, said Juan Xavier Sanchez, head of wealth strategy at Activest Wealth Management in Aventura, Florida. When rates are down and treasuries aren't paying good yields, people tend to be more risk-seeking for higher returns. "Bitcoin for many investors is in that bucket," Sanchez said. Experts have noted that gold, which is now down over 35% from its early 2026 peak, is less attractive when cash accounts are paying 5%. Investments like gold and bitcoin offer no yield. Bitcoin's rising correlation with the Nasdaq-100 since late September suggests the two are increasingly moving in tandem, according to data from Fairlead Strategies, a technical research firm. That's consistent with an environment of higher volatility in which correlations across risk assets tend to increase. However, the correlation remains below its early-2026 highs, the data show. Bitcoin has certain characteristics of digital gold, in that it has a limited supply, no single owner and no CEO or board that can decide to issue more, said Anthony Georgiades, founder and general partner at Innovating Capital in New York, which invests in early-stage crypto, blockchain, digital infrastructure and deep tech companies. But it's also been caught up in monetary policy since its inception. The last decade or so of monetary policy has been extremely rewarding to speculative risk-on assets, Georgiades said. However, in periods of volatility, those types of assets have experienced the most significant drawdowns and have been the most heavily punished, Georgiades said. That means that a shock on one side of the board that might be completely independent of bitcoin could trigger a large volatility event "given how intertwined digital assets have become in the overall financial system," he said. Notably, bitcoin hasn't acted much like digital gold in more recent years, said Abe Sheikh, chief investment officer of Cordoba Advisory Partners in New York. In fact, it has fallen substantially during periods when the stock market has been falling. For example, from October 6 through November 18, the S&P 500 fell about 6.3%, and bitcoin fell around 27%. From January 21, 2025 through April 8, 2025, the S&P dropped around 17.4%, while bitcoin slid 27.8%, he said. Democrats gaining control over both houses is viewed as a negative for crypto from a market perspective. The crypto industry spent more than $200 million to support crypto-friendly candidates, but its role had less of an impact on overall results than in the last election cycle. However, bitcoin's downward trend was already in the works, said Cyrus Amini, chief investment officer at Hyphen Wealth Management in Lafayette, California. In September, the Clarity Act failed in the U.S. Senate, and while its outlook is now dim , according to many political and market experts, some form of crypto legislation is still considered a priority for many Democrats and Republicans, while the Trump-appointed heads of the Commodity Future Trading Commission and Securities and Exchange Commission continue to favor crypto in rulemaking. This fall, investors also started to question the security of encryption technology, leading to more concerns over the security of their bitcoin holdings, said Kirkley of Global Settlement Network. The Binance hack in October muddied the waters further. And the recent stock market jitters and economic concerns piled on doubts, Kirkley said. The last few weeks have been especially rough with data security concerns from multiple fronts, he added. Wall Street's embrace of bitcoin has been a big positive for the cryptocurrency. Kirkley noted that 20% of bitcoin's market price is coming from institutional investors, and that's a conservative estimate. In addition, new research from digital assets company Galaxy shows that a record 40.5% of all 13F-reported spot bitcoin exchange-traded product holdings, and 11.2% of all the bitcoin in the funds, came from advisory and wealth planning firms, such as RIAs and brokerage platforms, as of the third quarter 13F filings with the SEC, which are required of firms with over $100 million in assets to report their holdings. Much of this investment is through bitcoin spot ETFs like the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) that track its price. These ETFs, first approved by the SEC in January 2024, were supposed to provide a reliable new source of institutional demand. But ETF ownership also makes bitcoin especially easy to sell. Outflows from several of these funds have been substantial in recent months. IBIT, the largest of its peers, had six-month net outflows of $1.65 billion through Nov. 18 and one-month outflows of $1.37 billion, according to ETF Database. The second biggest, Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund ( FBTC ) had one-month net outflows of $322.65 million and six-month net outflows of $771.86 million, according to ETF Database. Grayscale Bitcoin Mini Trust ETF ( BTC ) had one-month net outflows of $66.35 million, though it had inflows of $590.04 million over six months. As of September 2026, public companies collectively hold close to 1.29 million bitcoins, which is more than 6% of the 21 million coins in existence, according to bitcoin.com . Most public companies invest their corporate treasury portfolios in low-risk, highly liquid instruments such as money market funds, Treasury bonds and Treasury bills. That said, there are some well-known companies that have invested in bitcoin. SpaceX, for example, purchased 18,712 bitcoins for a total cost of $661 million, at an average price of $35,324 per coin. The company began accumulating bitcoin in early 2021 and held its position unchanged from mid-2024 until its IPO filing . Digital Asset Treasury companies, known as DATs or DATCOs, have also played a role in bitcoin's volatility . DATs are publicly listed firms whose primary business strategy involves holding significant quantities of digital assets, such as bitcoin or ethereum , on their corporate balance sheets to drive shareholder value. Companies in this space include Strategy , Strive, and Twenty One Capital. "DATs have exacerbated the problem," said Sheikh of Cordoba Advisory Partners. When bitcoin is rising, these companies borrow money in the debt market or raise capital to buy more bitcoin, which magnifies the upswings. They have also sold bitcoin to make their bond coupon payments. "It leads to enormous volatility on the upside and downside," Sheikh said. As of mid-November, Strategy, the largest corporate holder of bitcoin, holds 850,849 BTC, according to a regulatory filing . That represents roughly 4% of bitcoin's total supply. The company acquired these holdings at a total cost of approximately $64.2 billion, with an average purchase price of roughly $75,452 per coin, according to the filing. Bitcoin has been trending lower since the peak in October 2025. A trading range has taken hold and the bottom of the range is just below 60,000, said Katie Stockton, founder and managing partner of Fairlead Strategies. "It appears to be trying to find a footing," she said. Oversold conditions on the heels of recent lows in June and July, in addition to long-term momentum, suggest bitcoin can support an upturn, she said. But that depends on whether the crypto can hold at a current range around $60,000, she said. "At the end of the day, bitcoin is exceptionally volatile. It's still an area that people might go to sell when they think that risk is higher in other areas." By mid-morning Friday, the price of bitcoin had slipped below $60,000, its lowest mark since July. It was on pace for its seventh-straight weekly loss for the first time since May 2022, according to CNBC data.

extraction.body: Bitcoin fell sharply on Thursday, dropping below $85,000 for the first time in nearly two months, as a broad pullback in risk assets swept through global markets and intensified pressure on cryptocurrencies. The world’s largest digital asset slid as much as 5.7% to $84,233, its lowest level since Dec. 1. The decline marked a significant breakdown after weeks of sideways trading and underscored the fragility of sentiment across the crypto market. Losses were even steeper among smaller tokens, with Ether, XRP, Dogecoin, Cardano and Solana all falling by 6% or more. The sharp move lower in prices triggered a wave of forced selling across crypto derivatives markets. Around $785 million worth of digital assets were liquidated over the past 24 hours, according to data compiled by Coinglass. More than half of those liquidations occurred in just the last four hours, reflecting the speed at which losses cascaded as key technical levels were breached. The latest drop extended a broader downturn that has persisted in crypto markets since early October. Bitcoin prices had largely stagnated in recent weeks, even as technology stocks and precious metals such as gold and silver rallied. That divergence broke down abruptly, however, as cryptocurrencies began to mirror a wider selloff in risk assets. Technology stocks led the decline, with Microsoft shares collapsing more than 11%, a move that would rank as their worst one-day fall since March 2020. The selloff followed the company’s report of slowing growth in its cloud business and dragged the Nasdaq Composite lower by roughly 1.5%, reinforcing a risk-off tone across markets. The pressure was not limited to equities. Precious metals, which had surged to record highs, also reversed violently. Gold, which had briefly climbed above $5,600 per ounce earlier in the session — having never traded above $5,000 before Sunday night — plunged nearly 10% within minutes during US morning trade, falling back below $5,200. Silver followed a similar trajectory, sliding from around $121 per ounce to $108. Bitcoin exchange-traded funds have also come under strain. So far this week, bitcoin ETFs have recorded $160.1 million in net outflows, according to data from SoSoValue, extending a pattern of capital leaving the products amid market turbulence. Julio Moreno, head of research at CryptoQuant, said the recent pullback represents the first meaningful stress test for bitcoin ETFs since their rapid growth last year. Moreno noted that cumulative ETF flows peaked at $72.6 billion on Oct. 10, 2025, and have since seen $6.1 billion in net outflows. That reduction has cut ETF holdings to about $66.5 billion, representing an 8.4% drawdown from the peak. “If price holds above ETF realized price, it gives this cohort a reason to stay invested. If it fails, ETF flows risk shifting from passive consolidation into active distribution. Right now, Bitcoin is trading at the line where ETF conviction is tested,” Moreno wrote. When Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) reported on Nov. 17, its fiscal third-quarter revenue had more than doubled from the year before, to a record $115.8 billion. But for memory investors, the more telling number was how much the artificial intelligence (AI) chip leader has agreed to pay its suppliers. Nvidia 's supply commitments rose to $390 billion, up from $279 billion a quarter earlier. And the company said the increase was "primarily related to the multi-year procurement of memory supply." Missed AI’s "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we’re only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » That's good news for Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) , one of the three big makers of the memory chips Nvidia buys. But Micron stock is around $702 as I write, about 42% under the record $1,213.56 it closed at on June 25. I think the market's underrating what Nvidia's report says about Micron's business. Showing how fast its buying has picked up, Nvidia's supply commitments have more than tripled over two quarters. They were at $119 billion as of April 26, climbed to $279 billion by July 26, and hit $390 billion by Oct. 25, the end of its fiscal third quarter. In both of the last two quarters, the company linked most of the rise to memory. What's more, the money's coming due sooner. Of the $390 billion, $203 billion falls in Nvidia's fiscal 2028, which ends in January 2028. Three months earlier, that year's figure was $87 billion. In short, Nvidia is locking in memory long before it needs the chips, and much of this spending will probably land within about a year. Nvidia doesn't say how it splits the spending between its memory suppliers. SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics sell Nvidia high-bandwidth memory (HBM), too. (HBM is the stacked memory that sits next to AI processors.) Micron doesn't name its largest buyers, either. However, no single customer made up 10% or more of its revenue for its fiscal 2026, which ended Sept. 3, down from one customer at 17% the year before. So Micron's direct sales to Nvidia, whatever they are, were under a tenth of its revenue last year. What Micron does say is encouraging. It's working with Nvidia on what it calls the industry's first custom HBM4E chip, designed for Nvidia's next generation of graphics processing units . And its cloud memory business unit, which sells HBM to all data center customers, keeps growing. It pulled in $16.3 billion of revenue in the three months ended Sept. 3, up 18% from the previous quarter and more than triple the $4.5 billion of a year before, with an 83% gross margin. On its fiscal fourth-quarter call, Micron said it had lifted its HBM prices significantly for calendar 2027. Nvidia's commitments look like the buyer's side of a change Micron is already building its business around. Micron has now signed 26 multiyear strategic customer agreements, up from 16 a quarter earlier. All are take-or-pay deals, so customers commit to buying fixed volumes and can lose deposits if they fall short. Customers have committed $32 billion under the deals, mainly as cash deposits, compared to the $22 billion Micron forecast a quarter before. Micron also puts its remaining performance obligations (contracted sales it hasn't recognized yet) at around $150 billion, counting just committed volumes at minimum prices. "[E]ven at floor prices, we expect margins meaningfully above any prior cycle peak margins," chief financial officer Mark Murphy said in Micron's prepared remarks for the fiscal fourth quarter. But the stock trades like the boom might end soon. At around $702, Micron's price-to-earnings ratio is about 4 based on analysts' estimates for fiscal 2027 (which ends next September), and only about 9 on fiscal 2026's actual earnings of $74.33 per share. When Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) reported on Nov. 17, its fiscal third-quarter revenue had more than doubled from the year before, to a record $115.8 billion. But for memory investors, the more telling number was how much the artificial intelligence (AI) chip leader has agreed to pay its suppliers.
Nvidia 's supply commitments rose to $390 billion, up from $279 billion a quarter earlier. And the company said the increase was "primarily related to the multi-year procurement of memory supply."

Missed AI’s "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we’re only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

That's good news for Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) , one of the three big makers of the memory chips Nvidia buys. But Micron stock is around $702 as I write, about 42% under the record $1,213.56 it closed at on June 25.
I think the market's underrating what Nvidia's report says about Micron's business.

Showing how fast its buying has picked up, Nvidia's supply commitments have more than tripled over two quarters. They were at $119 billion as of April 26, climbed to $279 billion by July 26, and hit $390 billion by Oct. 25, the end of its fiscal third quarter. In both of the last two quarters, the company linked most of the rise to memory. What's more, the money's coming due sooner. Of the $390 billion, $203 billion falls in Nvidia's fiscal 2028, which ends in January 2028. Three months earlier, that year's figure was $87 billion.

In many ways, Taiwan Semiconductor , or TSMC, is the gatekeeper of the AI boom, because without it, the breakneck growth of Nvidia, Micron, and other AI-related companies would not be possible. TSMC does pretty much one thing: It makes chips and semiconductor components for other companies, like Nvidia and Micron. That's why it is called a foundry -- a term that refers to a factory where things are manufactured. As a semiconductor foundry, it is dominant, making about 70% of all chips and roughly 90% of more advanced AI semiconductor chips. Its major customers include Nvidia, as well as other tech stock giants like Apple , Broadcom , Advanced Micro Devices , and Amazon , to name a few. TSMC makes millions of advanced chips every year and will generate some $33 billion from its largest customer, Nvidia, in 2026. Nvidia could not produce that many advanced chips that quickly without TSMC. Its technologies and processes set it apart from competitors, and it stands alone in its ability to make the most advanced chips at such scale, speed, and cost. This is why Taiwan Semiconductor is so indispensable to Nvidia. TSMC does not play the same role for Micron, but it is just as valuable to the memory chipmaker. While TSMC doesn't make memory chips for Micron, it makes the components that are required for Micron's advanced, next-generation high bandwidth memory (HBM) chips, which are used for AI applications. As with Nvidia, TSMC's advanced technologies and processes are needed for these faster, more advanced HBM chips, and Micron could not make them as quickly or at such a scale without TSMC. In addition, Micron partners with TSMC to package the next-generation HBM chips using TSMC's CoWoS (chip-on-wafer-on-substrate) technology. Nvidia and other chip companies use TSMC packaging for their AI processors, which includes essential foundational wafers, or base dies, provided by TSMC to make the stack function. Micron signed an agreement with TSMC to produce the base die for these stacks, enabling them to adopt this architecture alongside Nvidia and others. So, without its connections to TSMC, it would not have access to the advanced components for its next-generation memory chips nor to TSMC's AI architecture stacks. passages: Nvidia 's supply commitments rose to $390 billion, up from $279 billion a quarter earlier.
And the company said the increase was "primarily related to the multi-year procurement of memory supply."
In both of the last two quarters, the company linked most of the rise to memory.
Three months earlier, that year's figure was $87 billion.
Of the three companies selling Nvidia its memory, Micron is the one I'd buy.
It's working with Nvidia on custom HBM, and unlike Samsung, it's a pure memory and storage business.
Micron's customers have made $32 billion in financial commitments under its multiyear supply deals.
Nvidia's commitments look like the buyer's side of a change Micron is already building its business around.
Sure, memory prices have crashed before, and Micron plans to spend more on new plant space, which might loosen supply in late 2028 and beyond.
But a growing share of its sales now comes with committed volumes, deposits, and price floors, protections Micron didn't have in past memory busts.
Micron also puts its remaining performance obligations (contracted sales it hasn't recognized yet) at around $150 billion, counting just committed volumes at minimum prices.
Nvidia doesn't say how it splits the spending between its memory suppliers.
SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics sell Nvidia high-bandwidth memory (HBM), too. (HBM is the stacked memory that sits next to AI processors.)
So Micron's direct sales to Nvidia, whatever they are, were under a tenth of its revenue last year.
The Motley Fool has positions in and recommends Micron Technology and Nvidia.
I think the market's underrating what Nvidia's report says about Micron's business.
In short, Nvidia is locking in memory long before it needs the chips, and much of this spending will probably land within about a year.

facts.text: Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) both make chips that are essential to the continued AI build-out, but their chips couldn't be more different.
Nvidia makes advanced logic chips and graphics processing units (GPUs) used for training and inference of large language models.
While Micron prints its chips itself, Nvidia contracts chip manufacturing to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing .
However, there's one company neither could produce its chips without: Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT).
The company supplies manufacturers such as Micron and Nvidia's partner, TSMC, with a wide range of wafer fabrication equipment.
That's despite heavy spending from advanced logic chipmakers like TSMC as well.

passages: Source : WhatsApp Patches 3 Security Flaws, Including Android Bug Suspected of Use in Scams , by The Hacker News , The Hacker News , Nov 20, 2026
WhatsApp patched three security vulnerabilities, including an Android flaw the company suspects scammers used to make fraudulent messages look credible.
The first flaw, CVE-2026-23871, affects WhatsApp for Android and WhatsApp Business for Android before version 2.26.17.4.
It involves incomplete validation of external ad-reply URLs.
An attacker could send media from an attacker-controlled URL in a crafted Click to WhatsApp ad-reply message.
WhatsApp said someone may have used the flaw with specific spam messages.
The company's security team discovered and reported the issue.
A WhatsApp spokesperson said the team found the flaw while disrupting a scam campaign and believes a scammer used it to make scam messages seem more credible.
WhatsApp did not disclose the scale of the activity or whether those efforts succeeded.
The tap can delete files stored on the device.
An actor positioned inside Meta infrastructure could bypass the hardware root of trust with a Versioned Chip Endorsement Key (VCEK) certificate not signed by the hardware manufacturer's key.
Someone would first need to publish that certificate to the third-party binary transparency ledger that WhatsApp Private Processing uses.
WhatsApp advises users to keep apps and devices updated.
The company said it keeps strengthening its systems and acknowledged the bug bounty community's contributions to platform security.
Atredis Partners built three fuzzing campaigns for GStreamer's MP4 demuxer and found nine memory-safety flaws.

extraction.body: Meta-owned WhatsApp patched three security vulnerabilities, including an Android ad-reply flaw the company suspects scammers used to make messages look credible. WhatsApp patched three security vulnerabilities, including an Android flaw the company suspects scammers used to make fraudulent messages look credible. The first flaw, CVE-2026-23871, affects WhatsApp for Android and WhatsApp Business for Android before version 2.26.17.4. It involves incomplete validation of external ad-reply URLs. An attacker could send media from an attacker-controlled URL in a crafted Click to WhatsApp ad-reply message. When WhatsApp displayed that message in a thread, the attacker could learn the target's IP address. WhatsApp said someone may have used the flaw with specific spam messages. The company's security team discovered and reported the issue. A WhatsApp spokesperson said the team found the flaw while disrupting a scam campaign and believes a scammer used it to make scam messages seem more credible. WhatsApp did not disclose the scale of the activity or whether those efforts succeeded. The second flaw, CVE-2026-102769, is an SQL injection vulnerability in WhatsApp for Android before version 2.26.35.74. It occurs when a recipient taps a crafted "order details" message sent from an unofficial client. The tap can delete files stored on the device. An attacker could learn one bit about the user's chat database through an induced-crash delivery receipt timing side channel if the user is online when the malicious message arrives. WhatsApp said it found no evidence that anyone exploited the flaw in the wild. The third flaw, CVE-2026-44908, is a trust-validation vulnerability in WhatsApp's certificate verification mechanism for Meta AI's confidential computing infrastructure. It affects WhatsApp for iOS before version 2.26.24.72, WhatsApp Business for iOS and WhatsApp for Mac Desktop before version 2.26.23.72, WhatsApp for Android before version 2.26.23.74, and WhatsApp Business for Android before version 2.26.23.70. An actor positioned inside Meta infrastructure could bypass the hardware root of trust with a Versioned Chip Endorsement Key (VCEK) certificate not signed by the hardware manufacturer's key. Someone would first need to publish that certificate to the third-party binary transparency ledger that WhatsApp Private Processing uses. WhatsApp said the ledger shows every published VCEK certificate chains to the hardware root of trust, which confirms no exploitation. WhatsApp advises users to keep apps and devices updated. The company said it keeps strengthening its systems and acknowledged the bug bounty community's contributions to platform security. The update changes how PHP handles session IDs, cookies, and null bytes. A flaw in Linux KVM, tracked as CVE-2026-99312, lets a guest VM read host memory on AMD systems with nested virtualization enabled. Operators running their own KVM hosts need to patch the host kernel or disable nested virtualization. Atredis Partners built three fuzzing campaigns for GStreamer's MP4 demuxer and found nine memory-safety flaws. The work shows why naive mutation fails on nested MP4 atoms and how targeted structure-aware fuzzing recovers coverage. extraction.body: Meta-owned WhatsApp has addressed security vulnerabilities, including one impacting its Android app that it suspects may have been exploited in connection with scam messages. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-23871 , has been described as a case of incomplete validation of external ad-reply URLs in WhatsApp for Android and WhatsApp Business for Android before 2.26.17.4. The issue could have "caused a target's device to reveal its IP information to an attacker if an attacker sent media from an attacker-controlled URL when a crafted Click to WhatsApp ad-reply message was rendered and displayed in a message thread," WhatsApp said. The messaging platform said it may have been "abused in conjunction with specific spam messages." Internal researchers on the WhatsApp Security Team have been credited with discovering and reporting the issue. When reached for comment, a WhatsApp spokesperson told The Hacker News that the vulnerability was discovered while disrupting a scam campaign. "We believe a scammer was using it to make their scam message seem more credible," the spokesperson added. WhatsApp did not disclose the scale of the activity, and if those efforts were successful. Also addressed by the company are two other flaws - Interestingly, CVE-2026-102769 is also capable of leaking one bit of information through a timing-based side channel if the user is online at the time of receipt of the malicious message. It "leaked one bit of information asked by the attacker about the user's chat database via an induced-crash delivery receipt timing side channel," WhatsApp added. There is no evidence the vulnerability has been exploited in the wild. Successful exploitation of CVE-2026-44908, on the other hand, could have allowed a bad actor positioned within Meta infrastructure to bypass the hardware root of trust using a Versioned Chip Endorsement Key ( VCEK ) certificate not signed by the hardware manufacturer's key. "Any such VCEK Cert would first have to be published to the third-party binary transparency ledger used by WhatsApp Private Processing," WhatsApp noted. "The ledger shows that every published VCEK certificate chains to the hardware root of trust, confirming no exploitation." WhatsApp is advising users to keep their apps and devices up to date to ensure optimal protection. The company also said that it continuously works to strengthen its systems and acknowledged the bug bounty community's contributions towards keeping the platform secure. An attacker could learn one bit about the user's chat database through an induced-crash delivery receipt timing side channel if the user is online when the malicious message arrives. WhatsApp said it found no evidence that anyone exploited the flaw in the wild. The broader digital asset market has struggled after the Clarity Act, a crypto market structure bill, failed to advance in the Senate in September.

"I think the biggest catalyst we're seeing right now is actually very much in motion and it's happening, which is capital markets are moving onchain," eToro CEO Yoni Assia told CNBC in an exclusive interview from the conference.
He pointed to the SpaceX IPO as an example, which had derivatives trading on eToro before the IPO.
That includes BlackRock , the world's largest asset manager.
Last month, Strategy's Michael Saylor said he thinks bitcoin's next bull market is already underway.
Wood said that ARK Invest believes bitcoin has found its low and stressed that cybersecurity is "top of mind right now," which could provide yet another opportunity for crypto markets to rebound.
Crypto investors are hunting for the next positive catalyst after U.S. crypto regulation — a longtime market driver — fizzled in 2026.
Assia said that supportive regulation in the U.S. from agencies, including the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, is also helping adoption of crypto.

extraction.body: Crypto investors are hunting for the next positive catalyst after U.S. crypto regulation — a longtime market driver — fizzled in 2026. Bitcoin traded around $61,500 on Friday, a more than 50% decline from its all-time high above $126,000 reached in October 2025. The broader digital asset market has struggled after the Clarity Act, a crypto market structure bill, failed to advance in the Senate in September. Investors now see Wall Street's embrace of blockchain technology — particularly tokenization — as the next trend to give bitcoin a boost. "Every single traditional firm is now looking at digital assets," BitGo CEO Mike Belshe told CNBC last week in an exclusive interview from the fintech-focused Cantor Convergence conference in Miami Beach. That includes BlackRock , the world's largest asset manager. He pointed to statements from the asset management giant's CEO, Larry Fink, who said the next major evolution in global finance is the creation of digital representations of every stock, bond, fund and real-world asset onto a shared blockchain ledger. "I think the biggest catalyst we're seeing right now is actually very much in motion and it's happening, which is capital markets are moving onchain," eToro CEO Yoni Assia told CNBC in an exclusive interview from the conference. He pointed to the SpaceX IPO as an example, which had derivatives trading on eToro before the IPO. "First day of trading, we distributed it to our retail clients, and it started trading 24/7, and that's all because capital markets are now copying crypto markets and are sitting on the same rails," Assia said. "Crypto markets have always been 24/7, they never sleep, and now what we're seeing is that capital markets are copying crypto markets using the same technology so stocks are moving onchain, they're being tokenized." Assia said that supportive regulation in the U.S. from agencies, including the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, is also helping adoption of crypto. He pointed to the CFTC earlier this month clearing the way for crypto-style perpetual futures tied to individual stocks to trade on regulated U.S. exchanges for the first time. Assia also highlighted the SEC's move to issue an order in September, creating a regulatory pathway for certain trading venues to trade tokenized representations of publicly traded U.S. stocks. "Blockchain technology is now starting to power what's happening in capital markets," Assia told CNBC. "That is the one of the biggest changes we're going to see in capital markets for many, many years." "We're talking about hundreds of trillions of dollars that are going to be tokenized and move onchain and at the same time, I do believe that will support prices of bitcoin and other blockchains as well," he continued. The industry is also watching whether inflation will ease and geopolitical tensions will subside in the new year, which could lower broader macro risk currently hampering the industry. Last month, Strategy's Michael Saylor said he thinks bitcoin's next bull market is already underway. ARK Invest Chief Investment Officer Cathie Wood told CNBC the investment management firm's $1.5 million bull case price target for bitcoin by 2030 still stands. She also said that it wouldn't surprise her if bitcoin reached its all-time high again before the end of 2027. "Our macro forecast has inflation breaking down considerably," Wood told CNBC in an exclusive interview at Cantor Convergence. "I think the elections have increased our confidence there because the war [in Iran], one way or the other, is going to end." She added that "bitcoin has weathered so much bad news," including the $6.3 billion Binance hack and the "distraction" of AI which, "many people would say is sucking the oxygen away from bitcoin." The maturation of the artificial intelligence trade could provide an opportunity for bitcoin to find new inflows. Wood said that ARK Invest believes bitcoin has found its low and stressed that cybersecurity is "top of mind right now," which could provide yet another opportunity for crypto markets to rebound. "I think if the Bitcoin and crypto world coalesces and makes investors feel that they've got their arms around security and actually understand that there might be more security issues in the traditional financial system, I think we're going to see a wave of support," Wood said. coreStoryFacts.text: ARK Invest Chief Investment Officer Cathie Wood told CNBC the investment management firm's $1.5 million bull case price target for bitcoin by 2030 still stands.
She also said that it wouldn't surprise her if bitcoin reached its all-time high again before the end of 2027.
The broader digital asset market has struggled after the Clarity Act, a crypto market structure bill, failed to advance in the Senate in September.

"I think the biggest catalyst we're seeing right now is actually very much in motion and it's happening, which is capital markets are moving onchain," eToro CEO Yoni Assia told CNBC in an exclusive interview from the conference.
He pointed to the SpaceX IPO as an example, which had derivatives trading on eToro before the IPO.
That includes BlackRock , the world's largest asset manager.
Last month, Strategy's Michael Saylor said he thinks bitcoin's next bull market is already underway.
Wood said that ARK Invest believes bitcoin has found its low and stressed that cybersecurity is "top of mind right now," which could provide yet another opportunity for crypto markets to rebound.
Crypto investors are hunting for the next positive catalyst after U.S. crypto regulation — a longtime market driver — fizzled in 2026.
Assia said that supportive regulation in the U.S. from agencies, including the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, is also helping adoption of crypto.

extraction.body: Crypto investors are hunting for the next positive catalyst after U.S. crypto regulation — a longtime market driver — fizzled in 2026. Bitcoin traded around $61,500 on Friday, a more than 50% decline from its all-time high above $126,000 reached in October 2025. The broader digital asset market has struggled after the Clarity Act, a crypto market structure bill, failed to advance in the Senate in September. Investors now see Wall Street's embrace of blockchain technology — particularly tokenization — as the next trend to give bitcoin a boost. "Every single traditional firm is now looking at digital assets," BitGo CEO Mike Belshe told CNBC last week in an exclusive interview from the fintech-focused Cantor Convergence conference in Miami Beach. That includes BlackRock , the world's largest asset manager. He pointed to statements from the asset management giant's CEO, Larry Fink, who said the next major evolution in global finance is the creation of digital representations of every stock, bond, fund and real-world asset onto a shared blockchain ledger. "I think the biggest catalyst we're seeing right now is actually very much in motion and it's happening, which is capital markets are moving onchain," eToro CEO Yoni Assia told CNBC in an exclusive interview from the conference. He pointed to the SpaceX IPO as an example, which had derivatives trading on eToro before the IPO. "First day of trading, we distributed it to our retail clients, and it started trading 24/7, and that's all because capital markets are now copying crypto markets and are sitting on the same rails," Assia said. "Crypto markets have always been 24/7, they never sleep, and now what we're seeing is that capital markets are copying crypto markets using the same technology so stocks are moving onchain, they're being tokenized." Assia said that supportive regulation in the U.S. from agencies, including the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, is also helping adoption of crypto. He pointed to the CFTC earlier this month clearing the way for crypto-style perpetual futures tied to individual stocks to trade on regulated U.S. exchanges for the first time. Assia also highlighted the SEC's move to issue an order in September, creating a regulatory pathway for certain trading venues to trade tokenized representations of publicly traded U.S. stocks. "Blockchain technology is now starting to power what's happening in capital markets," Assia told CNBC. "That is the one of the biggest changes we're going to see in capital markets for many, many years." "We're talking about hundreds of trillions of dollars that are going to be tokenized and move onchain and at the same time, I do believe that will support prices of bitcoin and other blockchains as well," he continued. The industry is also watching whether inflation will ease and geopolitical tensions will subside in the new year, which could lower broader macro risk currently hampering the industry. Last month, Strategy's Michael Saylor said he thinks bitcoin's next bull market is already underway. ARK Invest Chief Investment Officer Cathie Wood told CNBC the investment management firm's $1.5 million bull case price target for bitcoin by 2030 still stands. She also said that it wouldn't surprise her if bitcoin reached its all-time high again before the end of 2027. "Our macro forecast has inflation breaking down considerably," Wood told CNBC in an exclusive interview at Cantor Convergence. "I think the elections have increased our confidence there because the war [in Iran], one way or the other, is going to end." She added that "bitcoin has weathered so much bad news," including the $6.3 billion Binance hack and the "distraction" of AI which, "many people would say is sucking the oxygen away from bitcoin." The maturation of the artificial intelligence trade could provide an opportunity for bitcoin to find new inflows. Wood said that ARK Invest believes bitcoin has found its low and stressed that cybersecurity is "top of mind right now," which could provide yet another opportunity for crypto markets to rebound. "I think if the Bitcoin and crypto world coalesces and makes investors feel that they've got their arms around security and actually understand that there might be more security issues in the traditional financial system, I think we're going to see a wave of support," Wood said. Bitcoin traded around $61,500 on Friday, a more than 50% decline from its all-time high above $126,000 reached in October 2025. The broader digital asset market has struggled after the Clarity Act, a crypto market structure bill, failed to advance in the Senate in September.
Investors now see Wall Street's embrace of blockchain technology — particularly tokenization — as the next trend to give bitcoin a boost.

"Every single traditional firm is now looking at digital assets," BitGo CEO Mike Belshe told CNBC last week in an exclusive interview from the fintech-focused Cantor Convergence conference in Miami Beach. That includes BlackRock , the world's largest asset manager.

He pointed to statements from the asset management giant's CEO, Larry Fink, who said the next major evolution in global finance is the creation of digital representations of every stock, bond, fund and real-world asset onto a shared blockchain ledger.

"I think the biggest catalyst we're seeing right now is actually very much in motion and it's happening, which is capital markets are moving onchain," eToro CEO Yoni Assia told CNBC in an exclusive interview from the conference. He pointed to the SpaceX IPO as an example, which had derivatives trading on eToro before the IPO.

"First day of trading, we distributed it to our retail clients, and it started trading 24/7, and that's all because capital markets are now copying crypto markets and are sitting on the same rails," Assia said. "Crypto markets have always been 24/7, they never sleep, and now what we're seeing is that capital markets are copying crypto markets using the same technology so stocks are moving onchain, they're being tokenized."
Assia said that supportive regulation in the U.S. from agencies, including the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, is also helping adoption of crypto.

He pointed to the CFTC earlier this month clearing the way for crypto-style perpetual futures tied to individual stocks to trade on regulated U.S. exchanges for the first time. Assia also highlighted the SEC's move to issue an order in September, creating a regulatory pathway for certain trading venues to trade tokenized representations of publicly traded U.S. stocks.

"Blockchain technology is now starting to power what's happening in capital markets," Assia told CNBC. "That is the one of the biggest changes we're going to see in capital markets for many, many years."

"We're talking about hundreds of trillions of dollars that are going to be tokenized and move onchain and at the same time, I do believe that will support prices of bitcoin and other blockchains as well," he continued.
The industry is also watching whether inflation will ease and geopolitical tensions will subside in the new year, which could lower broader macro risk currently hampering the industry.
Last month, Strategy's Michael Saylor said he thinks bitcoin's next bull market is already underway.

ARK Invest Chief Investment Officer Cathie Wood told CNBC the investment management firm's $1.5 million bull case price target for bitcoin by 2030 still stands. She also said that it wouldn't surprise her if bitcoin reached its all-time high again before the end of 2027.

"Our macro forecast has inflation breaking down considerably," Wood told CNBC in an exclusive interview at Cantor Convergence. "I think the elections have increased our confidence there because the war [in Iran], one way or the other, is going to end."
She added that "bitcoin has weathered so much bad news," including the $6.3 billion Binance hack and the "distraction" of AI which, "many people would say is sucking the oxygen away from bitcoin."
The maturation of the artificial intelligence trade could provide an opportunity for bitcoin to find new inflows.
Wood said that ARK Invest believes bitcoin has found its low and stressed that cybersecurity is "top of mind right now," which could provide yet another opportunity for crypto markets to rebound.

"I think if the Bitcoin and crypto world coalesces and makes investors feel that they've got their arms around security and actually understand that there might be more security issues in the traditional financial system, I think we're going to see a wave of support," Wood said.

story.title: Bitcoin's regulation bull case is played out. What could drive crypto gains moving forward - CNBC

facts.text: ARK Invest Chief Investment Officer Cathie Wood told CNBC the investment management firm's $1.5 million bull case price target for bitcoin by 2030 still stands.
She also said that it wouldn't surprise her if bitcoin reached its all-time high again before the end of 2027.
The broader digital asset market has struggled after the Clarity Act, a crypto market structure bill, failed to advance in the Senate in September.

"I think the biggest catalyst we're seeing right now is actually very much in motion and it's happening, which is capital markets are moving onchain," eToro CEO Yoni Assia told CNBC in an exclusive interview from the conference.
He pointed to the SpaceX IPO as an example, which had derivatives trading on eToro before the IPO.
That includes BlackRock , the world's largest asset manager.
Last month, Strategy's Michael Saylor said he thinks bitcoin's next bull market is already underway.
Wood said that ARK Invest believes bitcoin has found its low and stressed that cybersecurity is "top of mind right now," which could provide yet another opportunity for crypto markets to rebound.
Crypto investors are hunting for the next positive catalyst after U.S. crypto regulation — a longtime market driver — fizzled in 2026.
Assia said that supportive regulation in the U.S. from agencies, including the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, is also helping adoption of crypto.

extraction.body: Nothing founder Carl Pei recently teased a new device that won't feature a "new screen", nor was it possible to build as an app. So, what has his firm got up its sleeve? While there's no confirmation on that, the company has informed T3 that all will be revealed on 8 December 2026 – a week after Black Friday . All we know for now is that it will be an "AI device" and has been designed around "the context gap" – use cases for the AI systems we already have access to. The brand has also released a new teaser image, which looks a bit like a camera lens. Maybe the new device is an AI pin, a bit like the Plaud Note Pin or Meta's Muse Charm. Except this could also have a camera to peer at the outside world to add "context" to your requests and queries. Nothing has also been rumoured to be working on its own smart glasses too, like the Ray-Ban Meta pairs. That could also be a possibility. What it won't be is the Nothing Phone (4), although that could also see the firm switch more to an AI-centric operating system in future. Pei himself suggested a while back that he sees phones moving away from apps and more to agentic AI. Either way, the Nothing AI device is an interesting prospect – not least as it's launching at a strange time for an industry that tends to avoid the holiday season for the announcement of new products. In the west, at least. Chinese phone manufacturers are known to get ahead of rivals by unveiling new handsets at the end of each year – but mainly for China only. Still, considering Nothing's reluctance to keeping secrets, we're sure that we'll hear more about this new launch in the coming days. Expect a new tease or two, anyway.

Nothing founder Carl Pei recently teased a new device that won't feature a "new screen", nor was it possible to build as an app. So, what has his firm got up its sleeve?
While there's no confirmation on that, the company has informed T3 that all will be revealed on 8 December 2026 – a week after Black Friday .
All we know for now is that it will be an "AI device" and has been designed around "the context gap" – use cases for the AI systems we already have access to.

The brand has also released a new teaser image, which looks a bit like a camera lens. Maybe the new device is an AI pin, a bit like the Plaud Note Pin or Meta's Muse Charm. Except this could also have a camera to peer at the outside world to add "context" to your requests and queries.
Nothing has also been rumoured to be working on its own smart glasses too, like the Ray-Ban Meta pairs. That could also be a possibility.

What it won't be is the Nothing Phone (4), although that could also see the firm switch more to an AI-centric operating system in future. Pei himself suggested a while back that he sees phones moving away from apps and more to agentic AI.

Either way, the Nothing AI device is an interesting prospect – not least as it's launching at a strange time for an industry that tends to avoid the holiday season for the announcement of new products. In the west, at least.

Nothing founder Carl Pei recently teased a new device that won't feature a "new screen", nor was it possible to build as an app.

Either way, the Nothing AI device is an interesting prospect – not least as it's launching at a strange time for an industry that tends to avoid the holiday season for the announcement of new products.

What it won't be is the Nothing Phone (4), although that could also see the firm switch more to an AI-centric operating system in future.

extraction.body: Nothing founder Carl Pei recently teased a new device that won't feature a "new screen", nor was it possible to build as an app. So, what has his firm got up its sleeve? While there's no confirmation on that, the company has informed T3 that all will be revealed on 8 December 2026 – a week after Black Friday . All we know for now is that it will be an "AI device" and has been designed around "the context gap" – use cases for the AI systems we already have access to. The brand has also released a new teaser image, which looks a bit like a camera lens. Maybe the new device is an AI pin, a bit like the Plaud Note Pin or Meta's Muse Charm. Except this could also have a camera to peer at the outside world to add "context" to your requests and queries. Nothing has also been rumoured to be working on its own smart glasses too, like the Ray-Ban Meta pairs. That could also be a possibility. What it won't be is the Nothing Phone (4), although that could also see the firm switch more to an AI-centric operating system in future. Pei himself suggested a while back that he sees phones moving away from apps and more to agentic AI. Either way, the Nothing AI device is an interesting prospect – not least as it's launching at a strange time for an industry that tends to avoid the holiday season for the announcement of new products. In the west, at least. Chinese phone manufacturers are known to get ahead of rivals by unveiling new handsets at the end of each year – but mainly for China only. Still, considering Nothing's reluctance to keeping secrets, we're sure that we'll hear more about this new launch in the coming days. Expect a new tease or two, anyway.

What it won't be is the Nothing Phone (4), although that could also see the firm switch more to an AI-centric operating system in future. Pei himself suggested a while back that he sees phones moving away from apps and more to agentic AI.

Either way, the Nothing AI device is an interesting prospect – not least as it's launching at a strange time for an industry that tends to avoid the holiday season for the announcement of new products. In the west, at least.

facts.text: While there's no confirmation on that, the company has informed T3 that all will be revealed on 8 December 2026 – a week after Black Friday .
Still, considering Nothing's reluctance to keeping secrets, we're sure that we'll hear more about this new launch in the coming days.
Nothing founder Carl Pei recently teased a new device that won't feature a "new screen", nor was it possible to build as an app.

Either way, the Nothing AI device is an interesting prospect – not least as it's launching at a strange time for an industry that tends to avoid the holiday season for the announcement of new products.

sources.title: Bitcoin price today crashes near $59,000: Why Peter Brandt warns of a 75% correction as crypto market slid
passages: Ethereum has fallen nearly 6%, Solana has lost more than 7%, while Zcash has plunged 16.5% in the past 24 hours.BTC USD Outlook: Peter Brandt Warns of a Possible 75% Bitcoin CrashCould Bitcoin's latest decline turn into another prolonged bear market as Peter Brandt has raised that possibility by pointing to the scale of corrections seen after previous bull-market peaks.In a social media post on X, Brandt noted, Every bull market phase in BTC's history has ended with at least a 75% correction of the previous parabolic bull trend, and questioned, Could this be what's happening in Bitcoin?

According to CoinPaper's analysis, Bitcoin fell approximately 84% after its 2017 peak and around 77% during the 2021-2022 downturn.So a 75% fall from Bitcoin's October 2025 record of approximately $126,198 would take the price to around $31,550.

extraction.body: The bitcoin price crashed below $60,000 on Friday for the first time since early July, falling about $1,800 in roughly an hour as a deepening U.S. tech stock selloff dragged risk assets lower. Bitcoin traded near $61,400 at 9:40 a.m. ET and slid to about $59,600 by 10:45 a.m., a drop of nearly 3%, according to Look Into Bitcoin data . The bitcoin price is down about $3,400, or more than 5%, from the same time Thursday, when it traded near $63,000. The break of $60,000 is a key psychological level, and it came with little warning. Bitcoin price had held above $61,000 for most of the morning, even after a third straight daily loss. Wall Street opened sharply lower. The Nasdaq Composite fell more than 2% in morning trading as shares of Anthropic extended losses in its second day since a record Nasdaq debut. Nvidia and AMD also traded lower. Bitcoin has been moving with tech stocks. The market has questioned whether heavy spending on artificial intelligence will pay off, and Friday’s open did nothing to ease that worry. Rate expectations are adding pressure. Traders see a roughly 94% chance the Federal Reserve raises rates in December, CME Group’s FedWatch tool showed . Higher rates tend to hurt bitcoin and other assets that pay no yield. Earlier Friday, South Korea’s Kospi index fell more than 5% and chipmakers sank across Asia. That selling carried into U.S. trading and then into bitcoin. Some analysts had flagged $60,000 as a floor. Katie Stockton of Fairlead Strategies told CNBC the bottom of bitcoin’s trading range sits “just below 60,000,” and that it “appears to be trying to find a footing.” Friday’s drop tests that view. CoinShares head of research James Butterfill said this week the drop is a “continuation of the existing bear market.” His base case is range trading around $60,000 to $90,000 through much of 2027. JUST IN: Bitcoin falls below $60,000 for the first time since June. BTC is now less than 4% away from a new cycle low 👀 pic.twitter.com/GSZkbGdzZz Funds have been sellers. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) lost $541.1 million on Thursday, its biggest one-day outflow on record. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $582 million in total, extending a streak of heavy withdrawals this week. Leveraged traders were hit as well. More than $700 million in crypto positions were liquidated in the 24 hours before the latest drop, and about 86% were bets on higher prices. The slide below $60,000 likely forced out more of them. The move extends a month-long slump. Bitcoin has dropped roughly $20,000 in the past month, a slide tracked as the price fell under $62,000 on Thursday. Crypto stocks fell even faster. Strategy (MSTR) was down about 7% near $79.85, a day after it tumbled for a sixth straight session . Coinbase (COIN) fell about 3% to $105.36. Shares of Strive (ASST) fell to $15.31 Friday morning, down 21.47%, or $4.19, over the past five days. The stock has slid steadily from near $19.50 as bitcoin price’s sell-off deepened, with its sharpest drop in Friday’s trading. Bitcoin miners took the worst of it. MARA Holdings (MARA) dropped about 11% to $5.55. Riot Platforms (RIOT) lost about 11% to $15.85, and CleanSpark (CLSK) fell about 12% to $5.13. Data center operators that also mine bitcoin were hit hard. IREN fell about 12% to $12.62, and Cipher Digital (CIFR) dropped 14% to $5.58. Both have traded with AI stocks, which are also under pressure. The bitcoin price is now at its lowest since the first days of July. Bitcoin set its record above $126,000 in October 2025, so it has lost more than half its value from that peak. At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $59,600. passages: The bitcoin price crashed below $60,000 on Friday for the first time since early July, falling about $1,800 in roughly an hour as a deepening U.S. tech stock selloff dragged risk assets lower.

Bitcoin traded near $61,400 at 9:40 a.m. ET and slid to about $59,600 by 10:45 a.m., a drop of nearly 3%, according to Look Into Bitcoin data . The bitcoin price is down about $3,400, or more than 5%, from the same time Thursday, when it traded near $63,000.
The break of $60,000 is a key psychological level, and it came with little warning. Bitcoin price had held above $61,000 for most of the morning, even after a third straight daily loss.

Wall Street opened sharply lower. The Nasdaq Composite fell more than 2% in morning trading as shares of Anthropic extended losses in its second day since a record Nasdaq debut. Nvidia and AMD also traded lower.
Bitcoin has been moving with tech stocks. The market has questioned whether heavy spending on artificial intelligence will pay off, and Friday’s open did nothing to ease that worry.

Rate expectations are adding pressure. Traders see a roughly 94% chance the Federal Reserve raises rates in December, CME Group’s FedWatch tool showed . Higher rates tend to hurt bitcoin and other assets that pay no yield.
Earlier Friday, South Korea’s Kospi index fell more than 5% and chipmakers sank across Asia. That selling carried into U.S. trading and then into bitcoin.

Some analysts had flagged $60,000 as a floor. Katie Stockton of Fairlead Strategies told CNBC the bottom of bitcoin’s trading range sits “just below 60,000,” and that it “appears to be trying to find a footing.” Friday’s drop tests that view.
CoinShares head of research James Butterfill said this week the drop is a “continuation of the existing bear market.” His base case is range trading around $60,000 to $90,000 through much of 2027.
JUST IN: Bitcoin falls below $60,000 for the first time since June. BTC is now less than 4% away from a new cycle low 👀 pic.twitter.com/GSZkbGdzZz

Funds have been sellers. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) lost $541.1 million on Thursday, its biggest one-day outflow on record. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $582 million in total, extending a streak of heavy withdrawals this week.

Leveraged traders were hit as well. More than $700 million in crypto positions were liquidated in the 24 hours before the latest drop, and about 86% were bets on higher prices. The slide below $60,000 likely forced out more of them.
The move extends a month-long slump. Bitcoin has dropped roughly $20,000 in the past month, a slide tracked as the price fell under $62,000 on Thursday.

Crypto stocks fell even faster. Strategy (MSTR) was down about 7% near $79.85, a day after it tumbled for a sixth straight session . Coinbase (COIN) fell about 3% to $105.36. Shares of Strive (ASST) fell to $15.31 Friday morning, down 21.47%, or $4.19, over the past five days. The stock has slid steadily from near $19.50 as bitcoin price’s sell-off deepened, with its sharpest drop in Friday’s trading.
Bitcoin miners took the worst of it. MARA Holdings (MARA) dropped about 11% to $5.55. Riot Platforms (RIOT) lost about 11% to $15.85, and CleanSpark (CLSK) fell about 12% to $5.13.

Data center operators that also mine bitcoin were hit hard. IREN fell about 12% to $12.62, and Cipher Digital (CIFR) dropped 14% to $5.58. Both have traded with AI stocks, which are also under pressure.
The bitcoin price is now at its lowest since the first days of July. Bitcoin set its record above $126,000 in October 2025, so it has lost more than half its value from that peak.
At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $59,600.
